messages:
ryan: Quick heads-up — after the kernel-selector tweak in canary we saw ~15% tail latency regression on host ingress for p50->p99 under burst.
maria: ugh. which path? tokenization or the streaming path?
ryan: appears at the ingress boundary: small requests (<= 800B) that go through preparse -> grpc writev show extra syscalls. pprof and strace point at multiple writev / write calls per request.
kevin: did we change batching heuristics too? the selector change also moved some requests off the slim kernel.
ryan: yes, heuristic now groups by kernel fingerprint earlier which seems to split mini-batches more often. That combined with HTTP/2 framing leads to fragmented frames.
elena: can you paste the perf sample? curious if KV cache lookups are involved.
ryan: pasted below (sampling 30s on host-ingress):
```
  flat  flat%   sum%        cum   cum%
  0.45s  12.5% 12.5%     1.20s  33.3%  [kernel] writev
  0.35s   9.7%22.2%     0.35s   9.7%  ingress::serialize_small_frames
  0.30s   8.3%30.5%     0.30s   8.3%  http2::frame::write
  0.25s   6.9%37.4%     0.80s  22.2%  preparse::tokenize
```
kevin: that looks like we regressed on syscall count per request. Maybe the kernel diff increased number of fragments per request, causing writev to be called twice instead of once.
maria: also saw higher KV cache miss rate for those small traces — possibly because batch boundaries shifted, so kvcache keys are less likely to be hit.
elena: any strace snippet?
ryan: short extract:
```
writev(3, [{iov_base="...pt1", iov_len=384}, {iov_base="...pt2", iov_len=120}], 2) = 504
writev(3, [{iov_base="...hdr", iov_len=64}], 1) = 64
```
ryan: two syscalls where previously one combined buffer was issued.
kevin: maybe runtime does less aggregation of proto slices when kernel mismatch occurs. There's code in ingress serializer that prefers zero-copy and returns multiple iovecs unless "aggregate_small_frames" is true.
maria: can we toggle that flag in canary? quick experiment: set aggregate_small_frames=true for that host pool and rerun
ryan: already did: p99 improved from 132ms -> 112ms, p50 unchanged. But KV cache misses remained ~2% higher.
elena: so two issues: (1) writev fragmentation -> syscall overhead; (2) batch split causing kvcache cold misses. Both originate from kernel selection change.
kevin: for (2) we could teach the batching heuristic to prefer preserving batch alignment for requests that hit the same kvcache shard. e.g., include kvcache_shard in the routing fingerprint.
maria: risky to change kernel selector hot, but we can add a conservative opt: if request_size < 1k and previous route had aggregated frames, keep route until end-of-batch.
ryan: low-risk plan:
  - short-term: enable aggregate_small_frames on canary pools (done)
  - mid-term: add kvcache_shard to batching fingerprint to avoid unnecessary splits
  - long-term: adjust kernel selector to prefer unified path for small requests
elena: logging/telemetry needed to measure effectiveness. Add metrics: writev_calls_per_request, kvcache_miss_by_batch_alignment.
infra-bot: Deploy queued: rollout/aggregate-small-frames -> canary pool A (3 hosts). CI checks passed.
maria: also running a microbench harness (wrk variant) to simulate 2k rps, 60% small requests. will post numbers in 30m.
kevin: also adding a pprof endpoint to collect ephemeral traces per canary host for 5m windows.
ryan: FYI, here's the heuristic tweak proposal (pseudo):
```
if request.size < 1024 and chunking_mode == "streaming":
  prefer_kernel = last_used_kernel_for_worker
else:
  use normal fingerprint
```
elena: put that behind a feature flag and A/B it.
maria: agreed. if AB shows kvcache miss drop and tail latency improvement, roll.
kevin: I'll draft the change and tests. ping me if you want to pair on the kernel selector code path.
ryan: thanks all. I'll keep the canary watching and drop numbers here.
maria: thx — appreciate the quick triage :thumbsup:
